cues: Here is what the bulliform cells do.
On a hot afternoon in a Terai maize field, the plant loses water.
The bulliform cells lose turgor and shrink, and the leaf rolls inwards, upper side in.
A rolled leaf exposes fewer stomata to the dry air, and transpiration falls.
